books.name: fsent_champ_long_htfesmcl4
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the largest-return arm measured in this family, and registered because the owner asked for every arm to be visible rather than pre-filtered. It stacks the HTF-side FS entry (exp_htf_fs_entry=all) with max_consecutive_losses=4, which is the one setting that clears the 2022-H2 cell that the FS entry alone re-broke. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 793t / +917.80R / DD 27.74R / WR 43.0%, OOS 437t / +326.22R / DD 14.20R / WR 37.8%. ZERO negative half-years out of 12. THREE REASONS IT IS NOT THE RECOMMENDATION DESPITE THE NET. (1) In-sample drawdown 27.74R is at the owner's 29R budget ceiling, against 15.13R for fsent_champ_long_mcloff on less than half the return. (2) PERIOD CONTROL IS UNDERPOWERED OUT OF SAMPLE - b = +0.027 with t = 0.05 and MDE 1.16, i.e. the out-of-sample effect is indistinguishable from nothing, and the cluster bootstrap goes NEGATIVE at -0.03. (3) The FS entry collapses the flip/decisive/b2 regime buckets into one fs_entered set, so this arm stops distinguishing regimes - see method/HTF_FS_ENTRY_REJECTED.md. It buys +384R of in-sample return mostly by admitting 528 new trades rather than by improving the ones it had. Registered as the high-return end of the range so the owner can see what the ceiling costs. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0285 in sample, p = 0.5311 out of sample, gap +384.44 IS and +86.63 OOS - significant in sample, NOT out of sample. Significance means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's; it does NOT mean the book is statistically better in absolute terms, which the same audit shows it is not (the shipping book sits at the 58th and 45th percentile of a reshuffle of its own trades, and the corrected absolute null is M = 771.09R IS / 384.36R OOS against the 381.7 / 205.5 quoted in BASE_BOOK_NULL.md, which was measured on a different book). See method/NULL_AUDIT_P5.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mode_atr_low
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - blocked on drawdown against the owner's 20R budget, not on the invented 11.88R gate (withdrawn 2026-10-08 as mine, not the framework's). fsent_champ_long with mode='atr_low' - the atr_high inversion: decisive windows when 15m bars are QUIET, not big. Only the mode changes; every other knob identical. This is the strongest of the four on the framework's own buckets: it WINS bucket 1 outright in both eras - IS 641t / +721.3R / expectancy 1.125 / PF 3.22 against the base 528t / +533.4R / 1.010 / 3.09, and OOS 315t / +280.7R / 0.891 / 2.96 against 311t / +239.6R / 0.770 / 2.69 - on MORE trades than the base, so more evidence and not less. Its out-of-sample tail is also the healthiest in the set (top 5% contributes 71.2% against the base's 81.1%; removing the top 10% still leaves -4.6% against -11.7%; removing the top 5% leaves 26.3% against 16.3%) and its DD expansion is 0.51, i.e. half its out-of-sample drawdown is in-sample. It is blocked purely on bucket 2 and bucket 9: 28.9R max DD in sample against the owner's 20R budget, 82 trades to make the drawdown, 460 trades underwater against the base's 286, and a 16-trade losing streak against the base's 11. Its own threshold swept 0.20-0.60 and the OOS gain peaks sharply at 0.35 (+41.1R) and is NEGATIVE everywhere else - one point, not a region, which is exactly the grid-peak failure P69 warns about. This is the one candidate worth keeping open, and the open question is whether a 20R budget can stretch to 29R - the owner's call, not the registry's. See method/OWNER_SCORECARD_MODES.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mcloff_htf15
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the best NON-degenerate arm found, and the two findings that actually changed the picture, stacked. It is fsent_champ_long_mcloff (max_consecutive_losses=0) on the htf15 1h swing series. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 560t / +616.17R / DD 15.13R / WR 41.1%, OOS 299t / +277.35R / DD 13.64R / WR 38.1%. It beats the parent in BOTH eras by more than mcloff alone (+82.80R IS, +37.76R OOS) and beats mcloff in both eras as well (+49.59R IS, +6.44R OOS), for 1.00R of extra in-sample drawdown. ZERO negative half-years out of 12. WHY THIS IS THE RECOMMENDATION AND NOT htf15 OR htfesmcl4: it does not use exp_htf_fs_entry, so it keeps the flip/decisive/b2 regime buckets distinct and is NOT the degenerate all-fs_entered configuration that the completion sweep's highest arms all turn out to be. The 12-arm joint grid over max_consecutive_losses x HTF leg length x HTF FS entry produced a +1321.41R arm, and that arm collapses the regime distinction - see method/HTF_FS_ENTRY_REJECTED.md. This one reaches +616.17R while staying honest about what a regime is. PERIOD CONTROL, run on this exact combination on 2026-10-09: SURVIVES with b > 0 in 2 of 2 eras - b = +0.77 (t = 1.72, MDE 0.88) IS and b = +0.62 (t = 1.60, MDE 0.76) OOS, cluster bootstraps +0.80 and +0.64 - but it is UNDERPOWERED, and this is the honest cost of the extra swing. fsent_champ_long_mcloff on its own is the only arm in the family whose control is powered in BOTH eras, at t = 3.37 and t = 3.97. Adding the htf15 swing buys +49.59R IS and dilutes the cohort variance at the same time, so the recommendation on EVIDENCE remains mcloff and the recommendation on RETURN is this one. Still NOT adopted: no arm in the family has forward evidence, and 12 observations of a half-year table is not a guarantee. See method/RESEARCH_COMPLETE.md and method/GRID_PERIOD_AND_KNOB_GUARD.md. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0115 in sample, p = 0.1445 out of sample, gap +82.80 IS and +37.76 OOS - significant in sample, NOT out of sample - the era that matters. Significance means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's; it does NOT mean the book is statistically better in absolute terms, which the same audit shows it is not (the shipping book sits at the 58th and 45th percentile of a reshuffle of its own trades, and the corrected absolute null is M = 771.09R IS / 384.36R OOS against the 381.7 / 205.5 quoted in BASE_BOOK_NULL.md, which was measured on a different book). See method/NULL_AUDIT_P5.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mcloff
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - and the best-EVIDENCED one in the registry. It changes ONE INTEGER: max_consecutive_losses from 3 to 0, which turns the loss-run cutoff OFF. The autopsy of the parent's negative half-year found 2025-H1 was not a disaster but a coin flip that landed red: 60 trades, net -0.69R, mean -0.011R per trade, 20 winners making +29.6R against 40 losers making -30.3R. In that exact situation the cutoff is not protecting the book, it is cutting winners - it stops the book right before the recovery trade that follows every streak. MEASURED against the parent 528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS and 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS: IS 575t / +566.58R / DD 15.13R / WR 39.7%, OOS 337t / +270.91R / DD 14.16R / WR 37.1%. IT DOMINATES THE PARENT ON RETURN IN BOTH ERAS (+33.21R IS, +31.32R OOS) on 47 and 26 MORE trades, for 1.71R and 2.28R of extra drawdown. ZERO negative half-years out of 12. PERIOD CONTROL IS THE REASON TO TRUST IT - this is the only arm in the whole family whose effect is SIGN HOLDS and POWERED in BOTH eras: b = +1.21 (t = 3.37, MDE 0.70) IS and b = +1.86 (t = 3.97, MDE 0.92) OOS, cluster-bootstrap b_boot +1.28 and +1.92. Compare fsent_champ_long_htf15 (underpowered), fsent_champ_long_biasmom05 (b NEGATIVE and significant at t = -9.63 OOS) and htf_fs=all (underpowered). Still NOT adopted: the period control compares this arm to champ_long, NOT to absolute zero, and a book that is meaningfully better than its parent can still be negative in some unseen half-year. The cutoff also has a real purpose under position sizing, which is a risk decision and not a signal decision. Forward evidence does not exist for it yet. See method/MAXCONSEC_LOSSES_FINDING.md. PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book, 2026-10-10 (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.0312 in sample, p = 0.0117 out of sample, gap +33.22 IS and +31.32 OOS - the only book in the family significant in BOTH eras. Significance means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's; it does NOT mean the book is statistically better in absolute terms, which the same audit shows it is not (the shipping book sits at the 58th and 45th percentile of a reshuffle of its own trades, and the corrected absolute null is M = 771.09R IS / 384.36R OOS against the 381.7 / 205.5 quoted in BASE_BOOK_NULL.md, which was measured on a different book). See method/NULL_AUDIT_P5.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_htf15
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the only arm found so far that fixes the shipping book's one negative half-year WITHOUT losing return, and it does so by moving a knob almost nobody has touched: the HTF swing length. THIS IS THE ONE FROM THE OWNER'S OWN RULE. Asked on 2026-10-09 for something that never goes negative - 'kabhi negative nahi hona chahiye' - the sweep of the HTF plane (1h swings, min_bars 10 -> 3..40) found that fsent_champ_long's single negative half-year, 2025-H1 at -0.7R, disappears at min_bars 13 and the net RISES from +773.0R to +796.5R (14) and +822.4R (15). MEASURED: IS 520t / +567.57R / DD 17.28R / WR 41.2%, OOS 280t / +254.88R / DD 16.86R / WR 37.1%. Against the parent that is +34.2R IS and +15.3R OOS on 8 and 31 fewer trades. WHY THIS IS NOT A GRID PEAK: the region around it is a genuine plateau, not a spike. min_bars 12 gives +783.5R but still 1 negative cell; 13 gives +787.6R with 0; 14 +796.5R with 0; 15 +822.4R with 0; 16 +746.1R with 0; 18 falls back to +708.7R with 1 negative again. By contrast min_bars 30 posts the single best number in the whole sweep at +847.3R with 0 negative - and is a SPIKE: 24 gives +645.4R with 2 negatives, 28 gives +659.6R with 2, 32 gives +696.3R with 0, 34 gives +562.5R. A 200R peak with a 60R trough either side is not an edge, so 30 is rejected and 15 is kept. WHAT CHANGED MECHANICALLY: the HTF plane is engine slot 2 and its swing series feeds the leg ratio, the bias-momentum breaks, the bias flips and _sw_ts_dir_mag, which is the flip/decisive classification every trade is tagged with. A longer 1h leg means fewer, larger HTF windows - 1601 swings at min_bars 10 down to 1479 at 15 - so the regime the router sees is coarser and it sits on fewer regime flips. That is why it is a genuinely different book rather than a re-tuned one. NOTE ON REGISTRATION: the HTF swing length is NOT an engine parameter, it is the registry's `swing` FIELD selecting a precomputed series, so this book needs the `htf15` series added to run_experiment.get_data - it is there, built at min_bars=15 on the 1h flow candles. A book that wanted a different HTF length would need its own series there, not a params edit. STILL NOT ADOPTED: period control gives b=+0.5681 IS and +0.3723 OOS, both positive with 97-98% of the raw gap surviving the half-year fixed effect, so it is not a regime proxy - but both cells are UNDERPOWERED against their own MDEs (1.0372 and 0.8050), so the magnitude is not established. In-sample drawdown rises 13.42R -> 17.28R and OOS 11.88R -> 16.86R, which fits the owner's 29R budget but is a real cost. And the OOS window is 2021-22, which is not a holdout - see method/OOS_IS_NOT_A_HOLDOUT.md. See method/HTF_SWEEP_OWNER_RULE.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_mode_flip_quality
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - DISQUALIFIED 2026-10-08 as a regime proxy. fsent_champ_long with mode='flip_quality' - B2/flip by chop AND a HTF-magnitude floor, so it filters the chop branch. It held the base drawdown exactly (13.4R IS / 11.9R OOS) and was ahead on all three books of its family in the lane test (+4.8R / +4.8R / +54.0R), which is why it was the closest of the four. Period control then disqualified it: the mode is IN-SAMPLE INERT on all three books. In IS the arm and the base take the SAME trades - 0 new, 0 dropped on fsent_utcsat_long and fsent_champ_short, and on this book the entire +1.41R is ONE dropped trade - so all three IS cells are non-estimable and every R of the mode's effect is out of sample. Out of sample b after a half-year fixed effect is +0.2122 against an MDE of 0.8569: inside the noise floor, 96% of the raw gap explained by the calendar. The one powered cell is fsent_champ_short OOS (b +1.3963, t 2.016) - the FS-short mirror, a different architecture with 23.9R drawdown, and the source of the whole +54.01R - and one cell of one architecture on one era cannot carry the other five. The earlier 3-of-3 lane result was real and was not sufficient; being drawdown-neutral is not the same as being useful. Two corrections recorded on 2026-10-08: the 'fails on both second lanes (-7.0R, -4.1R)' sentence was measured on champion_multi_sw10/utcsat_multi_sw10, a DIFFERENT architecture (pivot_rule=origin, no FS side, no exp_mltf), and the first period-control harness labelled survivors as cohort=1, which produced a meaningless t of 7.672. Remains registered and pinned so the measurements are re-derivable. The branch also READS chop_thresh, which is not in this book's config, so it was never the base plus a mode string. See method/FLIP_QUALITY_PERIOD_CONTROL.md, method/MODE_CONFIRM2_RIGHT_LANES.md.

books.name: fsent_champ_long_causalfloor
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED. **The name is historical and wrong - this is NOT a causality fix, and nothing about it is a fix at all.** It is fsent_champ_long with one number changed: exp_window_floor_s, the wait between a window opening and the LTF entry being allowed, from the shipped 2700 seconds to 7200 seconds. That is the whole mechanism: a longer wait, not a corrected one. It came out of a sweep of that one parameter, 7200 was the best value found, and a value chosen by a sweep carries selection pressure - it was not derived from a rule.  IT WAS ORIGINALLY REGISTERED AS A CAUSALITY FIX AND THAT WAS WRONG. The first description claimed the shipped gate let an LTF entry run up to 900 seconds before its 1h window candle closed, and that this book removed those trades. That claim was withdrawn on 2026-10-10 - the six trades it pointed at sit exactly on the boundary, where the 15m bar closes at the same instant the 1h window closes, which is legal. method/WINDOW_FLOOR_LEAK.md, which carried the finding, was deleted with it; this text is the correction. Read method/WITHDRAWN_WINDOW_LOOKAHEAD.md before believing anything here about causality.  MEASURED against the parent (528 / +533.37 / 13.42 IS, 311 / +239.59 / 11.88 OOS): IS 513 / +529.84R / DD 13.62R / WR 39.6%, OOS 308 / +248.90R / DD 11.88R / WR 38.0%. It earns LESS in sample and about the same out of sample - it gives up trades to buy a smaller drawdown, and on this evidence it does not buy enough.  The book does have ZERO negative half-years where the parent has one, but that is NOT a regime discovery and must not be read as one: across 155 half-year cells the 6 negative ones are indistinguishable from the 149 positive ones in loss concentration (35.2% vs 36.1%) and losing-streak length (8.3 vs 8.1). The same expectancy is landing slightly red, not a condition that can be filtered. That finding lives in method/PERIOD_2025H1_WHAT_HAPPENED.md.  FOR THE RECORD, since it bounds every causality claim in this family: a slack audit on 2026-10-10 (exp_window_slack_audit.py, 29 books, both eras, 22154 trades) measured the gap between each trade's decision instant and the close of its 1h window candle. The gate at unified.py:1034 is permissive by 900 seconds in principle, but ZERO trades anywhere in the family landed in that band - the distribution is 21992 trades at 900s or more of clearance, 147 exactly on the boundary, and none between. The shipping book is clean at 311 of 311. The 15 apparent violations are all fsent_champ_long_mode_union and are a REPORTING defect in that book's window_start field, not lookahead - see method/WINDOW_SLACK_AUDIT.md.  PAIRED PERMUTATION vs the shipping book (exp_null_audit.py, 4000 draws, seed 20261010): p = 0.7256 in sample, p = 0.0230 out of sample, gap -3.52 IS / +9.31 OOS - out of sample only, and negative in sample. Significance here means this arm's choice of trades is unlikely to be a reshuffle of the parent's. It does NOT mean the book is better in absolute terms; the same audit shows it is not. See method/NULL_AUDIT_P5.md.

books.name: fsent_sig_multi
books.desc: CANDIDATE, NOT ADOPTED - the strongest non-shipping result in the repo, and still not an adoption. fsent_sig_full's entire filter set (bias_momentum 0.8, fs_small_swing 6.0, trail_skip_n 2, weekends skipped, FS entry on shorts, ext_stop_r 3.0, halt on 3) with max_positions 1 -> 0, i.e. the single-slot gate removed and concurrency enabled. ONE value differs from fsent_sig_full; the other 15 are identical. WHAT IT IS, in plain terms: the same signals, and the book simply stops standing aside. Of 50 extra out-of-sample trades, 48 were taken while a serial position was already open and only 2 after it closed; 47 of the 50 joined a position in the SAME direction, so this is adding to an existing bet rather than hedging. Those extras earned +25.1R at a 46% win rate, against -0.3R given up on trades the serial book took instead. In sample the same mechanism gives 108 extras earning +186.2R for a net +188.8R. MEASURED: IS 329t / +484.59R / DD 13.39R / WR 45.6%, OOS 195t / +219.82R / DD 7.64R / WR 47.2%. Against the shipping book out of sample that is 92% of the net on 63% of the trades, at 64% of the drawdown, with a 10-point better win rate, and BOTH direction columns stay alive (+136.7R long, +83.1R short) which matters because the FS-side autopsy found the two families pointing in opposite directions. GATES: period control positive in both eras with 99% of the raw gap surviving, so this is NOT a regime proxy - the ATR% ceiling's signature does not appear. The half-year partition is 12 of 12. Tail dependence IMPROVES in every cell of both eras: removing the top 10 trades leaves 40.1% of in-sample profit against the parent's 22.0%, and 30.7% out of sample against 22.4%, which is the opposite of mode_union's 96%. WHY IT IS NOT ADOPTED - CORRECTED 2026-10-08, because the original reason was wrong. I previously wrote here that the out-of-sample magnitude is underpowered (b +0.3303 against an MDE of 2.1999) and therefore should not be adopted. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN. The 'OOS' era is 2021-01-01 to 2022-12-31 and IS is 2023-01-01 to 2026-09-13 - the OOS window is two years OLDER than the in-sample window and has been re-scored many times. It is not a holdout and never was, as method/FORWARD_TEST_PLAN.md states in its own second paragraph ('reused many times, not a holdout'). A power gate on that window is a real measurement of a real limitation OF THAT WINDOW and is not a forward verdict in either direction: it does not say this arm is bad, it says we have no forward data on it. THE CORRECT REASON THIS IS NOT ADOPTED: the adoption decision is BLOCKED ON FORWARD DATA, which does not exist on this machine. method/FORWARD_TEST_PLAN.md is ACTIVE with a hard boundary at 2026-09-13 10:03 IST and five pre-registered gates; it was scored once on 2026-09-25 and produced 5 trades and NO VERDICT (n<50); data/forward/bybit/ is not present locally now. This book is NOT on the contract's pre-registered candidate list, and because no forward window exists on disk nothing is burned - so it can be added before a new window starts, which is the cheapest high-value action available. The in-sample magnitude IS powered (b +2.1619, t +2.240, MDE 1.8920, month-cluster bootstrap +1.8501) and the 2021-22 magnitude is not (b +0.3303, MDE 2.1999); both are true and neither is a forward statement. The 2.16-vs-0.33 gap is a 2023-26 versus 2021-22 difference and should have been labelled as such when first reported. The tightest partition cells matter: 2021-H1 is +39.6 against +39.9 and 2021-H2 +35.8 against +40.5, so the FIRST out-of-sample half-year is worth almost nothing and the gain is concentrated in 2022-H1 and 2022-H2. DO NOT carry the in-sample +2.16R per trade as a forward expectation; the honest figure is roughly +0.33R and even that is not established. Concurrency shape: depth 5 in sample, 4 out, but 69% of entries happen with nothing else open, so this is the same book that occasionally takes a second position, not a crowded one. A cap of 3 costs 1.5R in sample, nothing out of sample, and lowers drawdown in both eras - a free bound on the tail. Two notes on measurement, both of which cost real time and are recorded so they are not repeated: the sibling sweep on the multi books returns BYTE-IDENTICAL results because those books carry exp_mltf=True, which bypasses the max_positions gate entirely in the harness - so this knob is inert on them and meaningful only on the serial sig book; and max_positions must be set alongside the regime knobs rather than alone, since a 0.40% min-stop floor on this book costs 4.1% of the long book's net in sample against 4.1% gained out of sample. See method/SIG_MULTI_STUDY.md.
